title: High-power perturbations preserve a fibre-dimension bound
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $a,b\in S$, and let $d\ge0$ be an integer. For $c\in S$, let $f_c:\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[t])$ [def-pc-scheme] be induced by the $R$-algebra map $R[t]\to S$ sending $t$ to $c$, where $R[t]$ is the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. If every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $f_a$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$, then there is an integer $n_0\ge0$ such that for every integer $n\ge n_0$ every fibre of $f_{a^n+b}$ has dimension at most $d$. Empty fibres, of dimension $-\infty$, are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok, statement and proof in the Weak relative Noether normalization section.

proof.text: For any coordinate $c\in S$, the same finite set of $R$-algebra generators generates $S$ over $R[t]$ with $t\mapsto c$. Thus each coordinate morphism is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], hence finite type. We use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] to compute every affine fibre as $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_{R[t]}\kappa(Q))$. Quotients and localizations below have the same finite-generation property (a localization adds the inverse of its inverted element).

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; affine setup throughout the proof

proof.text: Write $S=R[A,B,x_1,\ldots,x_m]/J$, with $A,B$ mapping to $a,b$, using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For the small directed poset of finitely generated subideals $J_\lambda\subseteq J$ put $S_\lambda=R[A,B,x_1,\ldots,x_m]/J_\lambda$ and let $a_\lambda,b_\lambda$ be the images of $A,B$. Sums give upper bounds, transition maps are surjective, and the colimit is $S$, since every relation lies in one such subideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound] to the constant base $R[t]$ and maps $t\mapsto a_\lambda$; their transition maps are surjective and they are finite type. A stage has all fibre dimensions at most $d$. It is finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For any $n$, the fibre ring for $a^n+b$ is a quotient of the corresponding stage fibre ring. A strict prime chain in the quotient lifts by inverse image to a strict chain in the stage ring, so its dimension cannot increase [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A threshold for the stage therefore works for $S$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; first reduction paragraph; Limits Tag 05M5

proof.text: For finitely presented $R\to S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] to the zero module. It gives a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, finite-type $\mathbf Z$-bases $R_i$, finite-type $R_i$-algebras $S_i$, and $S_j\cong S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ and $S\cong S_i\otimes_{R_i}R$. After a universe enlargement the index is small. Choose a common stage carrying representatives $a_i,b_i$. The maps $R_i[t]\to S_i$, $t\mapsto a_i$, form a system with surjective comparison maps: $R_j[t]\otimes_{R_i[t]}S_i\cong R_j\otimes_{R_i}S_i\cong S_j$. The first isomorphism sends $(r t^k)\otimes s$ to $r\otimes a_i^k s$ and the inverse sends $r\otimes s$ to $r\otimes s$. The colimit base is $R[t]$, by taking coefficients of each finite polynomial. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound] to get a stage with the bound $d$. Every $S_i$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$ by adjoining its generators to those of $R_i$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; second reduction paragraph; Algebra Tag 00R1 and Limits Tag 05M5

proof.text: A threshold at the stage in Step 3 passes to $R\to S$: for each exponent the ring map $t\mapsto a^n+b$ is the base change of $t\mapsto a_i^n+b_i$, using $R_i[t]\otimes_{R_i}R\cong R[t]$ and $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R\cong S$. At a point of any new fibre, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies its local dimension with that at the corresponding point of the old fibre. Each is at most $d$, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives the whole new fibre bound, including an empty fibre. We may therefore restrict the remaining argument to $R,S$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; end of second reduction paragraph; Morphisms Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change) and Topology Tag 0B7I

proof.text: Induct strongly on $\dim R$, simultaneously for every finite-type $\mathbf Z$ ring map and every $d\ge0,a,b$ satisfying the hypothesis. The dimension is a finite nonnegative integer for $R\ne0$: $R$ is a quotient of $\mathbf Z[z_1,\ldots,z_m]$. Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal (take its least positive element), which also makes $\mathbf Z$ Noetherian; [lem-trf-principal-ideal-ring-dimension-bound] gives dimension at most one, and [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] gives a finite polynomial dimension. Prime chains of a quotient lift strictly [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For $R=0$ its unital algebra $S$ is zero, and all fibres are empty; likewise $S=0$ is immediate. The induction hypothesis covers all nonzero bases of smaller dimension, with the same nonnegative $d$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; third paragraph: finite base dimension and induction setup

proof.text: At a fixed base dimension it suffices to handle $S$ a domain. Indeed $S$ is Noetherian: [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-noetherian] applies to a polynomial presentation over $\mathbf Z$, and an ideal in a quotient is generated by the images of generators of its inverse image. By [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal] there are finitely many minimal primes $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ of $S$. Each $S/P_i$ is a finite-type domain and its coordinate fibres are quotient fibres, hence satisfy the assumed bound. Their thresholds have a finite maximum. Every prime in a fibre ring contracts to a prime of $S$, which contains some $P_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. A strict prime chain in that fibre whose smallest prime contracts to a prime containing $P_i$ lies wholly in the closed piece for $S/P_i$. Thus the pieces cover the fibre and bound all its prime chains. This proves the desired transfer without the unnecessary normalization step of the source.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; reduction to an integral source; fourth and fifth paragraphs simplified by closed irreducible components

proof.text: For $S$ a domain replace $R$ by its image $R\prime\subseteq S$. The image is a finite-type $\mathbf Z$ domain, its dimension is at most that of $R$, and $S$ is still finite type over it. If $K=\ker(R\to S)$, coordinate fibres over primes $Q\subset R[t]$ not containing $K R[t]$ are empty: an element of $K$ maps both to zero in $S$ and to a unit in $\kappa(Q)$. Over primes containing $K R[t]$, the quotient identifies the residue field and fibre ring with those for $R\prime[t]$. Thus both the hypothesis and conclusion transfer exactly. If $\dim R\prime<\dim R$, apply the strong induction hypothesis already stated; otherwise solve the injective-domain case below at this same dimension. Combined with Step 6 this reduces the inductive step to $R\subseteq S$ domains.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; sixth paragraph: replace the base by its image

proof.text: We will use $\dim_z\mathbf A^r_k=r$ for $r=1,2$. A field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, so is Noetherian and has dimension zero. [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension], together with the spectrum equality in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], gives $\dim\mathbf A^r_k=r$. The polynomial ring is a domain; [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] says every nonempty open has that same dimension. Taking the minimum over neighbourhoods in [def-kun-dimension] gives the asserted local dimensions. Now put $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Apply [lem-trf-composite-fibre-dimension-inequality] to $X\xrightarrow{f_a}\mathbf A^1_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. At each point of $X_p$ its local dimension is at most $d+1$. [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim X_p\le d+1$ for every $p$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; integral affine case before the dominant/non-dominant dichotomy; Tag 02JS

proof.text: Let $\phi:X\to\mathbf A^2_R$ correspond to $x\mapsto a,y\mapsto b$, and let $\pi_n:\mathbf A^2_R\to\mathbf A^1_R$ send the target coordinate to $x^n+y$. Then $f_{a^n+b}=\pi_n\phi$. First suppose $R[x,y]\to S$ is injective. By [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation], applied to this finite-type map with integral target, there is a nonempty open $W\subseteq\mathbf A^2_R$ on which $\phi$ is flat. Choose a nonzero polynomial $H$ with $D(H)\subseteq W$; injectivity makes $H(a,b)\ne0$, so $U=D(H(a,b))\subseteq X$ is nonempty and $\phi|_U$ is flat. Its generic fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a nonempty open in the spectrum of the domain $S\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}R$: localization keeps $H(a,b)$ nonzero. It is dense. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-open-fibre-density] to $h$ and $U$ to obtain a nonempty open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ such that $U_p$ is dense in $X_p$ for every $p\in V$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; dominant case; Tags 052A and 054X

proof.text: Fix any $n\ge0$, a point $q\in\mathbf A^1_R$ over $p$, and a point $u\in U_q$. Let $z=\phi(u)$ and put $e=\dim_u(U_z)$. Apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] twice, with flat first morphism $\phi|_U$, once followed by $\mathbf A^2_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and once by $\pi_n$. The first target fibre is $\mathbf A^2_{\kappa(p)}$ with local dimension $2$. The second has coordinate ring $\kappa(q)[x,y]/(x^n+y-\tau)\cong\kappa(q)[x]$, where $\tau$ is the image of the target coordinate; the maps substitute $y=\tau-x^n$ and keep $x$. It has local dimension $1$ by Step 8. Consequently $\dim_u U_p=e+2$ and $\dim_u U_q=e+1$. Since $U_p$ is open in $X_p$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] and Step 8 give $e+2\le d+1$. Thus $\dim_u U_q\le d$, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim U_q\le d$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; dominant case: write the additive fibre-dimension calculation without needing composition-flatness

proof.text: For $p\in V$ let $Z_p=X_p\setminus U_p$, with its closed-subscheme structure. If $X_p$ is empty there is nothing to check. Otherwise it is finite type over the field $\kappa(p)$, hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] (a field is Noetherian), and has finite dimension at most $d+1$. The density in Step 9 makes $Z_p$ nowhere dense. [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] gives $\dim Z_p<\dim X_p\le d+1$, hence $\dim Z_p\le d$. For $q$ over $p$, the coordinate fibre on $Z_p$ has dimension at most $d$: its affine fibre ring over a prime of $\kappa(p)[t]$ is a localization followed by a quotient of the ring of $Z_p$, so prime chains lift. Denote this fibre by $Z_q$. Both $U_q$ and $Z_q$ are finite type over $\kappa(q)$: $U$ is principal open and $Z=X\setminus U$ is closed. The map $U_q\amalg Z_q\to X_q$ is surjective on points. A chain of irreducible closed subsets of the disjoint union lies in one summand, so its dimension is at most $d$. The image-dimension assertion of [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] now gives $\dim X_q\le d$. This proves the dense-base-open claim in the dominant case for all $n$, with $n_0=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; dominant case: closed complement and recombination of the two fibre pieces
Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; non-dominant case: the omitted degree calculation, including nonzero fibre values and the case g in R[x]

proof.text: Put $R_c=R[1/c]$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R_c[x,y]/(g))$, and factor $X_{D(c)}\to Y\xrightarrow{\rho_n}\mathbf A^1_{R_c}$. For $n>M$ and $q$ in the target, the fibre of $\rho_n$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(q)[x]/(g(x,\tau-x^n)))$, by the substitution of Step 12. A nonzero polynomial over a field has only maximal primes above it: divide by an irreducible factor to see that the corresponding quotient is a field (the Euclidean algorithm). Thus this fibre is empty or zero-dimensional; every local dimension is zero when nonempty. At a point $z\in Y$, the fibre of $X_{D(c)}\to Y$ is a quotient of the base change of the $f_a$-fibre at its image in $\mathbf A^1_R$: the extra coordinate imposes $b=y(z)$. [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] bound that base change by $d$, and prime chains show the quotient has the same upper bound. Apply [lem-trf-composite-fibre-dimension-inequality] to the displayed factorization and take the supremum of local dimensions. The fibres of $f_{a^n+b}$ over $D(c)$ have dimension at most $d$. This proves the dense-open claim in the non-dominant case with $V=D(c)$ and $n_0=M+1$.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; non-dominant case: make the conclusion from the polynomial calculation explicit; Tag 02JS

proof.text: In either case choose a nonzero $f\in R$ with $D(f)\subseteq V$; nonempty opens of an affine spectrum contain a basic open, and $R$ is a domain. The open-base bound then holds on $D(f)$. If $f$ is a unit this covers the base. Otherwise $R/fR$ has strictly smaller dimension: every prime chain containing $f$ begins with a nonzero prime, so adjoining the zero prime increases its length by one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The rings $R/fR$ and $S/fS$ are finite type over $\mathbf Z$. Their $a$-coordinate fibres over primes $Q\subseteq(R/fR)[t]$ are exactly the original fibres over the inverse-image primes in $R[t]$: both residue fields are the fraction field of the same quotient domain, and the tensor map sends $\bar s\otimes u$ to $s\otimes u$. Hence their hypothesis retains the bound $d$. Apply the strong induction hypothesis to obtain a threshold $n_1$. For dimension-zero domains a nonzero $f$ is a unit: otherwise a maximal prime containing $f$ would give a chain of length one. This supplies the base of the induction.

source.place: Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok; last paragraph: dimension decrease and induction on the closed complement

proof.text: Take $N=\max(n_0,n_1)$, omitting $n_1$ when the complement is empty. For each $n\ge N$ and prime $Q\subseteq R[t]$, set $p=Q\cap R$. If $f\notin p$, the fibre for $a^n+b$ is unchanged by inverting $f$, since $f$ is already a unit in $\kappa(Q)$; the tensor isomorphism is induced by $s/f^k\otimes u\mapsto s\otimes f^{-k}u$. The open-base bound applies. If $f\in p$, the fibre is $(S/fS)\otimes_{(R/fR)[t]}\kappa(Q/fR[t])$, canonically the original fibre as in Step 14; the closed-base induction bound applies. These two cases cover all target points, giving the threshold for the injective-domain case. Steps 6–7 give the threshold for all finite-type $\mathbf Z$ rings; Steps 2–4 give it for every finite-type $R\to S$ in the statement. Empty fibres satisfy the bound throughout.
